# Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: the wild three-adic BCDT route

This roadmap develops the independent Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor proof of modularity of every elliptic curve over Q. Its reusable outputs are explicit wild local types, ramified finite-flat model classifications and one-parameter tangent bounds. The global argument turns them into modularity of cyclotomic absolutely irreducible F₅ representations and then of rational elliptic curves. The elliptic modularity predicate and the modular parametrisation interface belong to **EllipticCurveModularity**; this Part II supplies another proof, without using that roadmap’s unconditional theorem or full Serre modularity.

The baseline is Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`. All nodes are specifications, with implementation status unchecked. The exact supplier contracts fix the shared arithmetic interfaces; the suggested-signature boundary identifies conditions that need those carriers.

## Conventions and boundaries

Write G₃=Gal(Q₃ˢ/Q₃), I₃ for its inertia subgroup, G_Q=Gal(Qˢ/Q), ε₃ for the three-adic cyclotomic character and ω for its reduction. Use the native absolute Galois group and its Krull topology. Representations and cohomology are continuous. The native `ContRepresentation` and `TopRep` carriers bundle continuous linear operators; arithmetic applications also require continuity in the group variable, expressed by joint continuity of the action or continuity to a finite discrete matrix group. Use the existing continuous-cohomology coefficient and restriction maps, not abstract-group cohomology.

Local reciprocity sends a uniformizer to **arithmetic Frobenius**. Residual local theorems are over F₃, and global mod-five modularity is over F₅. No theorem over an algebraic closure of either residual field is inferred. Très ramifié means the nonsplit cyclotomic extension has a nonzero valuation component in its Kummer class; the peu line is the unit line. Changing unramified quadratic twists is allowed only where the precise statement says so. A full extended Weil type records its uniformizer value in addition to inertia.

Finite-flat groups, Dieudonné modules and Breuil modules use the supplied **contravariant** convention. In the BCDT Breuil presentation S=k[u]/u^(3e), take N(u)=+u and cπ=−φ(G) for an Eisenstein polynomial uᵉ−3G(u); set φ=cπ⁻¹φ₁uᵉ. The wild descent formulas include the tγ and fγ,γ′ correction operators. They are not the tame semilinear descent formulas. The representation V and Dieudonné Verschiebung V_D are different objects. The relation F+V_D=0 together with FV_D=3 gives F²=−3.

S(V) consists of finite-length modules filtered with every graded piece isomorphic to the **whole nonsplit V**. It is not the category defined by the composition factors of V. A weakly filtered integral model has some closed-subobject filtration with the specified integral graded models. A strongly filtered model requires every generic V-filtration to induce such an integral filtration. These categories include all three-power torsion exponents. None is silently declared closed under all extensions.

Shared theories retain their owners. ClassFieldTheory supplies reciprocity, Kummer theory and local Tate duality; LocalFieldsRamification supplies local extension/valuation theory; FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory supplies the general wild Breuil and strong-filtration machinery; LocalGaloisDeformationRings supplies deformation rings and type quotients; GL₂ automorphic and lifting roadmaps supply compact-admittance and classical lifting; EllipticCurves supplies torsion/reduction and the cross-prime comparison; ModularCurves and ModularCurvesPartII supply actual twisted moduli curves and their connected/rational compactifications; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups supplies Hilbert irreducibility with local conditions. The exact additional contracts appear below. There is no plan here for higher-dimensional automorphy, arbitrary-coefficient Serre modularity, a new general Breuil theory, or a new definition of elliptic modularity.

The present upstream ModularCurves §5C makes geometric connectedness conditional; ModularCurvesPartII R12.4 discharges it. Current ProfiniteArithmetic and LocalGaloisGroups have been checked and supply neither these explicit wild field families nor the finite-flat calculations. Existing continuous cohomology, native intermediate fields, polynomial quotients and Weierstrass curves are used directly.

## W3.0. Wild types and simple admittance

Construct the cubic inertia types τ±1, ramified-quadratic types τ±3 and full extended Weil types τ′ᵢ (i∈Z/3), with arithmetic reciprocity and all unit/uniformizer values fixed. Compute the compact-type constituents and prove simple admittance for the appropriate prime-field F₃ very ramified residual representations. Retain the full G₃ hypothesis in the extended case.

**Supplier inputs:** `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`, `LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.3/bcdt-type-rings`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`.

### The cubic wild types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/cubic-types` · definition.

Fix an order-three matrix ζ in GL₂(Z₃). The Q₃-type τ₁ is the two-dimensional inertia representation corresponding by arithmetic reciprocity to the character of Z₃× with values −1↦1 and 4↦ζ. The type τ₋₁ is the representation obtained from the unramified quadratic field Q₃(j), j²=−1, whose unit character has values 4j↦1, 4↦1 and 1+3j↦ζ. These specify isomorphism classes, not chosen matrices or a finite-image Weil representation. Extend the inertia classes to Weil representations as in the supplier’s type definition.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Compute the relevant unit quotients using local reciprocity; the listed generators and relations determine the characters.
- 2. View the Q₃ character over its quadratic coefficient field as a two-dimensional representation; use induction/restriction for the unramified quadratic case.
- 3. Conjugating the order-three matrix replaces the realization without changing the type class.

**Direct prerequisites:** `LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.3/bcdt-type-rings`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Uses.**

- `W3.0/simple-admittance-cubic`: Select the compact-type constituents.
- `W3.3/cubic-weak-acceptability`: Match the local finite-flat condition to the characteristic-zero point quotient.

**API.**

- `cubicType_exists` (constructor): The listed unit values extend to the required continuous characters with open kernel.
- `cubicType_values` (simp): Evaluate τ₁ at −1 and 4, and the inducing character of τ₋₁ at 4j, 4 and 1+3j, with the values in the statement.
- `cubicType_independent_zeta` (equivalence): Replacing ζ by another order-three realization gives an isomorphic inertia type.
- `cubicType_weil_extension` (compatibility): The constructed objects meet the BCDT inertia-type predicate of R08.3; their associated compact types are the R16.3 objects, with the same arithmetic reciprocity convention.

**Unit tests.**

- `tauOne_four`: τ₁(Art₃(4)) has order three. This distinguishes the intended definition because: A trivial unit character fails.
- `tauMinusOne_four`: The inducing character of τ₋₁ is trivial on 4 and nontrivial on 1+3j. This distinguishes the intended definition because: The two cubic types cannot be interchanged.
- `tauMinusOne_frobenius`: The unramified quadratic conjugation inverts the cubic character. This distinguishes the intended definition because: A scalar two-dimensional character fails.

**Acceptance.**

- Both inertia images have order three; τ₋₁ has the nontrivial Frobenius conjugation on its cubic inertia image.

**Sources:** BCDT, §2.1, pp.860–861; §§3.1–3.2, pp.866–867.

**Planet:** Cubic wild types.

### The ramified quadratic wild types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/ramified-quadratic-types` · definition.

Let ζ have order three. The type τ₃ restricts to the unit character of Q₃(√3) with −1↦−1, 4↦1 and 1+√3↦ζ. The type τ₋₃ restricts to the unit character of Q₃(√−3) with −1↦−1, 4↦1, 1+3√−3↦1 and 1+√−3↦ζ. Use the unique two-dimensional Q₃ inertia-type class extending each restriction. These have order-six inducing characters and include the quadratic action, rather than treating the inducing character as a character of Q₃×.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Apply arithmetic reciprocity in the specified quadratic field, checking the unit relations.
- 2. Construct the corresponding rank-two type and show uniqueness of its class from the quadratic conjugation relation.

**Direct prerequisites:** `LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.3/bcdt-type-rings`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Uses.**

- `W3.0/simple-admittance-quadratic`: Identify the two one-dimensional U₀ constituents.
- `W3.4/quadratic-weak-acceptability`: Apply the local result to the two ramified quadratic types.

**API.**

- `quadraticWildType_exists` (constructor): The specified character and its rank-two inertia extension exist.
- `quadraticWildType_values` (simp): All generator values are the ones in the statement; in particular the τ₋₃ character is trivial on 1+3√−3.
- `quadraticWildType_unique` (characterisation): An inertia type with the indicated restriction is isomorphic to τ₃ or τ₋₃ respectively.
- `quadraticWildType_nativeType` (compatibility): These are instances of the supplier’s BCDT inertia type, with the R16.3 compact type and arithmetic normalization.

**Unit tests.**

- `tauThree_minusOne`: The inducing character takes −1 to −1. This distinguishes the intended definition because: Dropping the quadratic sign fails.
- `tauMinusThree_deepUnit`: The τ₋₃ character takes 1+3√−3 to 1. This distinguishes the intended definition because: Confusing it with an extended type fails.
- `tauThree_wildGenerator`: The τ₃ character takes 1+√3 to a nontrivial cube root of unity. This distinguishes the intended definition because: A tame type fails.

**Acceptance.**

- The value at −1 is −1, and the wild generator has order three in both families.

**Sources:** BCDT, §2.1, p.861; §3.3, p.867.

**Planet:** Ramified quadratic wild types.

### The conductor-243 extended types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/extended-types` · definition.

For i∈Z/3, let K=Q₃(√−3). The extended type τ′ᵢ is the rank-two Weil representation whose restriction to W_K corresponds under arithmetic reciprocity to the character of K× given by √−3↦ζ−ζ⁻¹, −1↦−1, 4↦1, 1+3√−3↦ζ and 1+√−3↦ζⁱ. Fix the full Weil isomorphism class, including its uniformizer value. Its inertia restriction has finite image, but the full Weil representation need not have finite image. In particular an unramified twist of the inertia restriction alone does not specify τ′ᵢ.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Check the inducing character on K×, including the uniformizer and unit relations.
- 2. Construct the irreducible Weil extension and compare it with the extended-type contract of R08.3 and the extended compact-type involution of R16.3.

**Direct prerequisites:** `LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.3/bcdt-type-rings`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Uses.**

- `W3.5/extended-weak-acceptability`: Keep the Weil point condition distinct from its inertial quotient.
- `W3.1/extended-local-frobenius-sign`: Identify the Frobenius sign on the local companion curve.
- `W3.6/global-companion`: Apply extended-type modularity lifting in the conductor-243 case.

**API.**

- `extendedWildType_exists` (constructor): The indicated character determines the extended rank-two Weil type τ′ᵢ.
- `extendedWildType_values` (simp): Evaluate the inducing character on all five listed generators.
- `extendedWildType_inertia` (projection): Restrict τ′ᵢ to inertia to obtain its BCDT inertia type, forgetting only the Frobenius datum.
- `extendedWildType_uniformizer` (characterisation): Among the extensions with the same inertia restriction, the value ζ−ζ⁻¹ at √−3 singles out this extended type class.
- `extendedWildType_compactInvolution` (compatibility): Its extended compact type includes the w₃ action used in simple admittance and in lifting Theorem 1.4.2.

**Unit tests.**

- `extendedWildType_uniformizer_square`: The square of the inducing value at √−3 is −3 in characteristic zero. This distinguishes the intended definition because: Assigning a root of unity to the uniformizer fails.
- `extendedWildType_deepUnit`: The inducing character takes 1+3√−3 to ζ, not to 1. This distinguishes the intended definition because: The τ₋₃ restriction fails.
- `extendedWildType_unramifiedTwist`: Multiplying the uniformizer value by −1 keeps the inertia restriction but does not give the chosen extended type. This distinguishes the intended definition because: An inertia-only definition fails.
- `extendedWildType_index`: At i=0,1,2 the value on 1+√−3 is 1,ζ,ζ² respectively. This distinguishes the intended definition because: Collapsing the three indices fails.

**Acceptance.**

- The determinant has the required arithmetic Frobenius normalization; the uniformizer value is retained in every characteristic-zero point condition.

**Sources:** BCDT, §2.1, equation (2.1.1), p.861; §3.4, pp.867–868.

**Planet:** Conductor-243 extended types.

### Simple admittance for the cubic types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/simple-admittance-cubic` · theorem.

For a continuous ρ̄:G₃→GL₂(F₃) whose inertia restriction is a très ramifié extension of ω by 1, both τ₁ and τ₋₁ simply admit ρ̄ in the exact BCDT §1.3 sense: there is a unique admitting Jordan–Hölder constituent, it occurs with multiplicity one, and that constituent simply admits ρ̄. With σₙ,ₘ=Symⁿ(F₃²)⊗detᵐ, the reduction for τ₁ has constituents σ₀,₀,σ₂,₀,σ₀,₁,σ₂,₁, the latter two of multiplicity one; the reduction for τ₋₁ has constituents σ₀,₀,σ₂,₁,σ₀,₁, the latter two of multiplicity one. The très ramifié condition excludes the peu branch in the n=0 admission rule.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. For τ₁ reduce the induced order-three character modulo three and calculate the Brauer constituents of induction from U₀(9); use induction in stages through U₀(3).
- 2. For τ₋₁ reduce induction from the nonsplit-torus congruence subgroup; compare the trivial, twisted-special and cuspidal summands using CDT Lemma 3.1.1.
- 3. Apply the supplied Serre-weight admission rules to the specified extension orientation, then check uniqueness and multiplicity one separately.

**Direct prerequisites:** `EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/cubic-types`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Acceptance.**

- A peu ramifié extension does not satisfy this theorem’s hypothesis.
- Merely finding a nonzero Hom is insufficient: the unique-constituent and multiplicity assertions must be proved.

**Sources:** BCDT, Lemma 2.1.1, p.861; §§3.1–3.2, pp.866–867; §1.3, pp.854–856.

**Planet:** Cubic simple admittance.

### Simple admittance for the quadratic types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/simple-admittance-quadratic` · theorem.

If ρ̄:G₃→GL₂(F₃) is continuous and its inertia restriction is a très ramifié extension of 1 by ω, both τ₃ and τ₋₃ simply admit ρ̄. Each compact type reduces to exactly σ′₀,₀ and σ′₁,₁ on U₀(3), each with multiplicity one; σ′ₘ₁,ₘ₂(diag(a,d))=aᵐ¹dᵐ². Apply the très admission rule rather than an unrestricted occurrence condition.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Use the index-two subgroup of U₀(3) defining each compact type.
- 2. Reduce its character and identify the two distinct characters of the quotient.
- 3. Use the extension orientation in the admittance rule to select the unique admitting constituent.

**Direct prerequisites:** `EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/ramified-quadratic-types`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Acceptance.**

- The compact reduction has two one-dimensional constituents, not a GL₂(F₃) symmetric-power decomposition.

**Sources:** BCDT, Lemma 2.1.3, p.862; §3.3, p.867; §1.3, pp.854–856.

**Planet:** Quadratic simple admittance.

### Simple admittance for the extended types

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/simple-admittance-extended` · theorem.

For every i∈Z/3 and continuous ρ̄:G₃→GL₂(F₃) that is a très ramifié extension of 1 by ω AS A G₃-REPRESENTATION, τ′ᵢ simply admits ρ̄. The constituents of its extended compact type are σ′_{ {0},1}, σ′_{ {1},1}, σ′_{ {0},−1}, σ′_{ {1},−1}; the latter two have multiplicity one. Here σ′_{ {m},a} restricts to σ′ₘ,ₘ and has w₃-eigenvalue a for w₃=((0,−1),(3,0)). In particular the trivial quotient character of ρ̄ has Frobenius value 1, selecting a=−1 in BCDT’s rule.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Compute the reduction of the extended compact induction, retaining w₃ rather than restricting to U₀(3).
- 2. Determine the four possible diagonal characters and their w₃ signs.
- 3. Apply the full G₃ admission rule with quotient Frobenius −a and prove the unique constituent has multiplicity one.

**Direct prerequisites:** `EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/extended-types`, `GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.3`.

**Acceptance.**

- An inertia-only hypothesis cannot replace the stated full G₃ hypothesis.
- The admitting constituent has w₃ sign −1 for the quotient character equal to 1.

**Sources:** BCDT, Lemma 2.1.5, p.862; §3.4, pp.867–868; §1.3, pp.855–856.

**Planet:** Extended simple admittance.

## W3.1. Splitting fields and local companion curves

Construct the five explicit Q₃ field families with normalized valuations, automorphisms, norm subgroups and wild Breuil correction polynomials. Give the six local F₅ character cases, prove their classification after a quadratic twist and construct paired local elliptic curves with the required very ramified three-torsion. Compute the extended uniformizer/Frobenius sign. The six proof cases are not a bijective list of conductor exponents.

### The cyclic cubic field

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.1/cubic-cyclic-field` · construction.

Let π be a root of X³−3X²+3. Put F₁=F′₁=Q₃(π). This is totally ramified cyclic of degree three, with π a uniformizer, and γ₃(π)=π²−2π generates its Galois group. The remaining root is 3+π−π². The Breuil coefficients are G(u)=u²−1, cπ=1−u⁶ in F₃[u]/u⁹, and Hγ₃=u−2.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Construct the field from the stated algebraic equations and prove the degrees using Eisenstein and the unramified quadratic extension.
- 2. Check the explicit generator maps, their orders and relations on the field generators; use the norm subgroup and local existence theorem to match the type’s splitting extension.
- 3. Compute the valuation of π and the Eisenstein data. Substitute the chosen generator maps into γ(π)/π to obtain H; check t and f through the supplier’s wild correction equations.

**Direct prerequisites:** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-3-ramification-the-tame-and-wild-cases-and-the-filtration`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`, `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, `mathlib:Padic`, `mathlib:IntermediateField.adjoin`, `EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/cubic-types`, `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`, `mathlib:AddValuation`.

**Uses.**

- `W3.2/local-categories`: Define the actual finite-flat descent base and special-fibre operator ideal.
- `W3.3–W3.5`: Supply the scalar and correction data for the explicit Breuil computations.

**API.**

- `cyclicCubic_minpoly` (data): The minimal polynomial of π is X³−3X²+3 and the other roots are π²−2π and 3+π−π².
- `cyclicCubic_uniformizer` (characterisation): The normalized integer valuation of π is one; [F₁:Q₃]=e=3 and f=1.
- `cyclicCubic_galois` (structure): The stated γ₃ is an automorphism of exact order three and generates Gal(F₁/Q₃).
- `cyclicCubic_breuilData` (compatibility): With the supplier’s N(u)=+u convention, G=u²−1, cπ=1−u⁶ and Hγ₃=u−2.

**Unit tests.**

- `cyclicCubic_roots`: Both displayed conjugates satisfy X³−3X²+3=0. This distinguishes the intended definition because: An incorrect sign in the automorphism fails.
- `cyclicCubic_constant`: G(0)=−1 and cπ(0)=1. This distinguishes the intended definition because: Forgetting the minus sign in cπ=−φ(G) fails.
- `cyclicCubic_order`: γ₃³(π)=π and γ₃(π)≠π. This distinguishes the intended definition because: A trivial descent generator fails.

**Acceptance.**

- All field equations, norm identities and generator relations hold on the actual extension; the ramification and residue degrees have the stated values.

**Sources:** BCDT, §6.1, pp.899–900.

**Planet:** The cyclic cubic field.

### The nonabelian cubic splitting field

`EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.1/cubic-nonabelian-field` · construction.

Let π³−3π²+6=0, let j²=−1, put F₋₁=Q₃(π) and F′₋₁=F₋₁(j). The cubic F₋₁/Q₃ is totally ramified, F′₋₁/F₋₁ is unramified quadratic, and Gal(F′₋₁/Q₃) is generated by γ₂ fixing π and negating j and by γ₃ fixing j and taking π to (jπ²−π+3(1−j))/2. Their orders are two and three, and γ₂γ₃=γ₃²γ₂. The Breuil data are G=u²−2, cπ=−1−u⁶, Hγ₂=1 and Hγ₃=((j−1)u²+(3−j)u−2)/4.

**Construction or proof.**

- 1. Construct the field from the stated algebraic equations and prove the degrees using Eisenstein and the unramified quadratic extension.
- 2. Check the explicit generator maps, their orders and relations on the field generators; use the norm subgroup and local existence theorem to match the type’s splitting extension.
- 3. Compute the valuation of π and the Eisenstein data. Substitute the chosen generator maps into γ(π)/π to obtain H; check t and f through the supplier’s wild correction equations.

**Direct prerequisites:** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-3-ramification-the-tame-and-wild-cases-and-the-filtration`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence`, `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, `mathlib:Padic`, `mathlib:IntermediateField.adjoin`, `EllipticCurveModularityWild3Adic:W3.0/cubic-types`, `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`, `mathlib:AddValuation`.

**Uses.**

- `W3.2/local-categories`: Define the actual finite-flat descent base and special-fibre operator ideal.
- `W3.3–W3.5`: Supply the scalar and correction data for the explicit Breuil computations.

**API.**

stages.title: Wild types and simple admittance
stages.description: Construct the cubic inertia types τ±1, ramified-quadratic types τ±3 and full extended Weil types τ′ᵢ (i∈Z/3), with arithmetic reciprocity and all unit/uniformizer values fixed. Compute the compact-type constituents and prove simple admittance for the appropriate prime-field F₃ very ramified residual representations. Retain the full G₃ hypothesis in the extended case.

stages.title: Splitting fields and local companion curves
stages.description: Construct the five explicit Q₃ field families with normalized valuations, automorphisms, norm subgroups and wild Breuil correction polynomials. Give the six local F₅ character cases, prove their classification after a quadratic twist and construct paired local elliptic curves with the required very ramified three-torsion. Compute the extended uniformizer/Frobenius sign. The six proof cases are not a bijective list of conductor exponents.

stages.title: Finite-flat conditions and tangent comparison
stages.description: Define the cubic finite-flat, quadratic Dieudonné-ideal and extended Dieudonné-ideal category conditions on the supplied ramified-descent generic fibres, for all three-power torsion levels. Construct Θ₀,Θ₁,Θω on continuous self-extension cohomology, prove the très ramifié common-kernel criterion and factor cubic/quadratic characteristic-zero type points through their category deformation rings.

stages.title: The cubic wild tangent calculations
stages.description: Compute the cubic rank-one descent models, forward and reverse extensions, rank-three lower-left vanishing and rank-four diagonal vanishing. Separate the fixed-determinant cyclic diagonal argument from the nonabelian all-extension calculation. Deduce the dimension-at-most-one category tangent bound and weak acceptability of τ±1 as a zero ring or quotient of O[[X]].

stages.title: The ramified-quadratic tangent calculations
stages.description: Compute the shared degree-twelve rank-one normal forms and adapted bases for the quadratic and extended fields. Prove the unique very ramified quadratic residual model, reversed push/pull vanishing and unramified diagonal image. Deduce tangent dimension at most one and weak acceptability of τ±3.

stages.title: Extended models and characteristic-three rings
stages.description: Construct and classify the four extended integral model pairs (2,6),(6,10),(2,10),(6,6), together with forward, reversed and diagonal generic Ext comparisons. Define their weak/strong singleton-filtered categories with coefficient actions. Prove all four tangent bounds, build the three compatible characteristic-three Artin families, and prove their whole deformation rings are F₃[[T]]. Then show every characteristic-zero extended-type point selects (6,6), and deduce extended weak acceptability.

stages.title: The independent three-five modularity argument
stages.description: Construct a rational five-level companion preserving the full local three-torsion and having surjective global three-torsion. Identify its six possible three-adic Tate types using elliptic cross-prime compatibility. Verify the exact classical modularity-lifting hypotheses in the five wild cases and the CDT tame branch. Prove modularity of absolutely irreducible cyclotomic F₅ representations, then modularity of all elliptic curves over Q by the two branches of CDT Theorem 7.2.4. Use the parent’s proof-independent conditional parametrisation interface.
